card.name: Wording of when to give a dose
card.fires_on: Words in administration instructions right after the drug name or verb, where timing comes next, such as "at least" before a meal, "once daily" or "before the antacid". It also fires on a few other words that precede a time or place phrase.

modes.label: Spacing from meals or other drugs
modes.description: Word just before "at least X hours before/after" a meal or interacting drug.
modes.example: Administer COBENFY orally at<< least>> one hour before a meal or at least

modes.label: Verb or drug name before schedule
modes.description: Administered, taken, or the drug name or tablets, just before frequency or timing wording.
modes.example: Nisoldipine extended-release tablets should be<< administered>> orally once daily.

modes.label: Comma after once daily
modes.description: Comma following "once daily" before time-of-day details.
modes.example: Escitalopram tablets should be administered once daily<<,>> in the morning or evening, with or

card.plain: It marks the spot in dosing directions where the text is about to say when to take the drug.
